title: Ivalue Infosolutions Ltd - 544523 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 gross sales rose 19.5% to INR 2,913.9 crore and normalised PAT grew about 20% to INR 102.3 crore; FY27 guided to 18-20% revenue and 20-22% PAT growth.
summary.overview: iValue reported FY26 gross sales of INR 2,914 crore (+19.5% YoY) and normalised PAT of INR 102.3 crore (+20%), excluding a one-time INR 5.2 crore Labour Code cost. Q4 gross sales were about INR 750 crore (+12% YoY), with Q4 gross margin of about 12.5% of gross sales, helped by year-end rebates and OEM pressure. Working capital improved to 30 net working capital days, and operating cash flow of INR 108 crore exceeded PAT for the first time. Management reiterated FY27 growth above FY26 and flagged possible dividend or buyback if no inorganic deal is done.

segments.name: Cybersecurity
segments.commentary: About 50% of gross sales and the fastest-growing segment in FY26; Q4 flat QoQ and +19% YoY. Growth focus includes AI security, LLM security and AI governance.

segments.name: Data Center Infrastructure (DCI)
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY and 25% QoQ in Q4; management calls it the primary growth engine, with AI data center and GPU infrastructure opportunities across BFSI, enterprise and government.

segments.name: ILM
segments.commentary: Declined 70% QoQ and 20% YoY in Q4 per management; no reason given on the call.

segments.name: ALM, Cloud and Others
segments.commentary: Up about 80% QoQ and about 10% YoY in Q4. Google Cloud order book exceeded INR 300 crore, with customer commitment of about INR 300 crore over 3-5 years, subject to workload-based upside.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: top-line growth of 18-20% and PAT growth of 20-22%, which management said it would maintain; FY27 expected to outperform FY26 on revenue and profitability.
Qualified opportunity book (CRM, not order book) of about INR 5,800 crore, with conversion of 30-35% (earlier cited around 25%).
Operating leverage: more than 70% of incremental gross margin expected to flow to EBITDA over the next two to three years (over 85% achieved in FY26).
Short-term gross margin view of around 10% on gross sales; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
Gross debt expected at INR 40-60 crore on a full-year basis, with Q1 seasonally higher.
Capital allocation: board evaluating inorganic deals; absent a deal, a dividend or buyback policy may follow this year or early next year.
Plans to enter select ASEAN markets on a measured basis; Middle East entry on hold due to current situation.
capex_capacity: Management said investments in manpower, office space and other needs for the next two to three years were made in the past one to two years.
Six new OEMs added over the last year; iValue has signed with 115 OEMs, more than 50 of them in cybersecurity.
Hardware is customised per customer order and placed with OEMs on order, so no hardware price inflation benefit was seen in Q4.
Inventory fell to INR 6 crore from INR 12 crore a year earlier.
demand_pricing: Customer decision cycles have become faster and COE-led integrated solutions have improved turnaround versus four to five years ago, lifting conversion.
Q4 margin lift attributed to back-end and volume rebates from OEMs and year-end negotiation with Indian OEMs.
Q1 FY26 margin dip (~6.8% on gross sales) came from deals struck in Q4 FY25 with forex and component cost changes that management absorbed.
Client mix: BFSI ~40% of business, government sub-20%, ITES and telecom together ~20%, others ~20%. Focus is mid-enterprise and above (around 5,000 users as a rough benchmark).
Management expects BFSI, cybersecurity, DCI and cloud to drive FY27 growth, with about seven to eight marquee deals in FY26 and similar expected in FY27.

FX: dollar-denominated OEM payables are hedged; customer quotes are valid for only a few days to limit exposure. Management says DCI could see component-availability delays, while cybersecurity supply is seen as steady.

qa_highlights.question: Were there large Q4 deals similar to the GSTN deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a little more than a couple of large deals were closed in Q4, billed and under execution, but declined to name the accounts.

qa_highlights.question: How is the adjusted ROCE of about 40% calculated?
qa_highlights.answer: ROCE is adjusted by deducting net cash of INR 212 crore from net worth before computing the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 segment growth rates?
qa_highlights.answer: QoQ: cybersecurity flat, DCI +25%, ILM -70%, ALM/cloud/others +80%. YoY: cybersecurity +19%, DCI +29%, ILM -20%, ALM/cloud/others about +10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 90 bps in FY26, and how is it set per deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 was the weak quarter (about 6.8% gross margin on gross sales vs 9.1% average) due to spillover from Q4 FY25 deals and FX and component cost changes. Margins are negotiated deal by deal with both customers and OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 5,800 crore a book-to-bill or order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a qualified opportunity pipeline in the CRM, not an order book, and the 30-35% conversion applies to it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT growth look like 10-12% against FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the like-for-like normalised PAT grew 20% (INR 85.3 crore to INR 102.3 crore). Including the INR 5.2 crore Labour Code exceptional, growth is about 15.5%.

risks_watch: Gross margin trajectory: Q4 was about 12.5%, but management guides to about 10% in the short term; Q1 has historically been weak.
ILM segment fell 70% QoQ and 20% YoY in Q4 with no explanation given.
Component and memory shortages could delay DCI deliveries despite management's view that OEMs and customers have adapted.
Rupee depreciation: management says hedging and short-validity quotes mitigate it, but the net impact on top line and EBITDA was not quantified.
Conversion of the INR 5,800 crore opportunity pipeline at 30-35% versus the earlier ~25% assumption.
Receivables recovery on a deal with a third-year instalment, now moving from long-term to short-term receivables (~INR 15 crore earlier).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY27 growth, with a clear focus on cash flow and working capital. Management was evasive on specifics: it declined to name Q4 large deals and deal sizes, to quantify the INR 5,800 crore pipeline, and to give a numeric FX sensitivity.
key_quotes: Our qualified opportunity book has reached up to INR 5,800 crores with conversion rates in the range of 30% to 35%.
This is the first time in iValue's history where we are able to showcase a cash flow from operations higher than our PAT.
Going forward, we believe that this operating leverage will sustain and at least more than 70% of the incremental gross margin will be coming down as an incremental EBITDA directly to us.

growth.why: FY27 guided to 18-20% top-line and 20-22% PAT growth (held), backed by a Google Cloud order book above INR 300 crore, a INR 5,800 crore qualified opportunity book at 30-35% conversion and DCI momentum, but no specific new capacity was quantified.
